capabilities.title: Stable element ids
capabilities.requirement: every element of the stand carries a stable id: the author's key where given, else its component path
capabilities.observed_gap: a node's id is a slot index plus a version; a remount re-clones nodes into fresh ids, and no semantic id exists — an agent can aim only at coordinates or selectors.

verification.acceptance: On each of the four lean stand tasks (counter, flight booker, timer, CRUD), booted by `seven_guis::stand` with `stand::options(false)` and `stand::options(true)`, `DioxusDocument::element_ids()` gives every element node of the document exactly one id, all pairwise distinct; an element whose HTML `id` is non-empty, `/`-free and the first of its value in document order reads that value verbatim (the TaskShell chrome and every lean-task control key), every other element reads its component path (the component names below the root, then `{tag}:{n}` / `{tag}[{key}]` element segments) or, outside every component (`html`, `head`, `body`), its document path `/html:0/…`; both layout modes read the same id list. Witness: `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_element_ids` (tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_element_ids.rs).

capabilities.notes: 2026-10-06 (2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits wrap): PREMISE CORRECTION, on the founder's ruling given at that chunk's phase (the founder, 2026-10-06; chunk inputs I1 · I2). This acceptance says every element that reads no author key "reads its component path … or, outside every component, … its document path". The id grammar now has a fourth tier between the author key and the component path: an unkeyed element under an element of its own component instance that reads an author key reads an anchored path, `{key}//{segment}` (architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge). On the four lean tasks at boot no element reads an anchored path (178 ids over both layout modes, measured at that chunk), and CRUD's three rows, which read `TaskShell/Crud/div:0/div:1/div:0/div[{n}]` when this capability was verified, now read their author keys `crud-person-0` · `crud-person-1` · `crud-person-2`, each row carrying an HTML `id`. The outcome is unchanged: every element node reads exactly one id, all pairwise distinct, both layout modes equal. The witness is the same test file, green with its row pin re-spelled (`stand_element_ids`, 4 passed). Status, ref and acceptance text are left as written. Record: escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits/report.md.

capabilities.title: Id persistence
capabilities.requirement: an element's id is identical across a re-render, a remount and a fresh process
capabilities.observed_gap: a node's id is a slot index plus a version; a remount re-clones nodes into fresh ids, and no semantic id exists — an agent can aim only at coordinates or selectors.

verification.acceptance:
On each of the four lean stand tasks (counter, flight booker, timer, CRUD), in both layout modes (stand::options(false) and stand::options(true)), DioxusDocument::element_ids() reads the same id for each element across a re-render, a remount and a restart in a new process. Witness: cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_id_persistence.
- Re-render: after each task's scripted re-renders (counter increments; flight booker's return toggle and Book, which inserts #flight-booked; delivered timer ticks; CRUD filter, Delete and Create), every element node present before and after reads the same id, and the DOM verifiably changed. A CRUD person's row keeps its id under a filter, after another person's Delete, and after a Create.
- Remount: in seven_guis::app::app booted with stand::options, after the task's card → Back → the same card, the id list equals the pre-remount list in order. Every element's NodeId differs from its pre-remount NodeId, except the four document-skeleton elements DioxusDocument builds outside the VirtualDom (/html:0, /html:0/head:0, /html:0/body:0, main), which keep theirs; every dropped pre-remount NodeId reads None. The pre-remount list equals stand::boot's for that task.
- Fresh process: a child process with a pid distinct from the parent's re-executes the test binary and reads, for each task and mode, a non-empty id list equal to the parent's.

capabilities.notes: 2026-10-06 PREMISE-CORRECTION (2026-10-06-id-persistence wrap): the Remount clause said "Every element's NodeId differs from its pre-remount NodeId, and every pre-remount NodeId reads None". That is false for the four document-skeleton elements (/html:0, /html:0/head:0, /html:0/body:0, main). DioxusDocument::new creates them outside the VirtualDom (packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs:104-129), so a task's remount never unmounts them: they keep their NodeId and still read their ids. Measured by stand_id_persistence::ids_hold_across_a_remount in both layout modes on the four lean tasks: the kept-NodeId set equals exactly those four; every other element's NodeId is fresh; every dropped pre-remount NodeId reads None. The clause is refined to name the exception; the outcome (the same id list in order across a remount, on fresh task nodes) is unchanged. Refined with evidence on the operator's decision at this wrap (operator, 2026-10-06). Evidence: escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-06-id-persistence/report.md (Spec claims disproved 2).

capabilities.title: Snapshot state fidelity
capabilities.requirement: snapshot state reflects enabled, checked, value and focused; a disabled control reads disabled, a typed value reads its value
capabilities.observed_gap: the screen is readable only as an HTML string, a debug tree print or a screenshot — large, noisy or lossy for an agent.

verification.acceptance: On the stand, in both layout modes, read through `DioxusDocument::snapshot`: a disabled control (`flight-return-date`, `flight-book` once a date is invalid, `crud-update`, `crud-delete`) reads `enabled: Some(false)` and reads `Some(true)` once the app enables it; after a pointer click on a text input, after a Tab key press and after Shift+Tab exactly the focused control reads `focused`, and with focus cleared none does; text typed through `click` and `type_text` into `crud-name`, `crud-surname`, `crud-filter` and `flight-start` reads back as that node's `value`. On the minimal fixture beside the stand (the founder's ruling, 2026-10-06 — the lean tasks hold no checkbox, radio or password input): a checkbox and a radio read `checked: Some(true)` after a real click and `Some(false)` before it; and a password's typed text occurs in no field of any snapshot node, its `value` reading the fixed mask `MASKED_VALUE`. Proved by `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_snapshot_state` passing its 7 tests.

capabilities.notes: 2026-10-06 (2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity, phase P5): claimed and concretized. The outcome-level acceptance is kept whole and made concrete per control; "a checked control reads checked" is proven on a minimal fixture beside the stand because the four lean tasks hold no checkbox or radio (the founder's ruling of 2026-10-06, carried on working-route lines 60 and 84); a password clause is added from the route entry (a typed password never appears in the snapshot — the fixed mask chosen at P4's question round, 2026-10-06). A select's value and a range input's interaction are outside the claim: the engine has no model for either (research.md).

capabilities.title: Id stability across code edits
capabilities.requirement: an element's id stays the same when the app's code is edited around it, not only across a re-render, a remount and a fresh process
capabilities.observed_gap: a node's id is a slot index plus a version; a remount re-clones nodes into fresh ids, and no semantic id exists — an agent can aim only at coordinates or selectors.

verification.acceptance:
On the stand — the four lean tasks (counter, flight booker, timer, CRUD), Home, and the edit fixture beside them in tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_id_edits.rs — each booted with `stand::options(false)` and `stand::options(true)`, an element left in place reads the same `DioxusDocument::element_id` before and after an edit of the code around it. The edit is a before/after pair: components of the same name in two modules, and an edited shell around the real lean-task components.
- Every element of each lean task reads the same id when the shell it is rendered in gains an earlier sibling of the task root's tag, a wrapper around the task and one more level.
- Every element that reads an author key reads the same id when a same-tag sibling is added before it, a sibling is removed, or an ancestor is wrapped.
- Every unkeyed element under a keyed element of its own component reads `{key}//{relative path}` and keeps it under every edit outside that keyed element.
- Every element reads the same id under an edit of text, an attribute, a class or a handler.
- The edits that may change an id are measured: an earlier same-tag sibling or a wrapper inserted between an unkeyed element and the point its path starts at changes that element's id and no keyed element's id.
- Every element an agent can act on — focusable, or carrying an interactive role, or carrying an event listener — reads an author key: `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable()` returns nothing on the four lean tasks and on Home, at boot and after Book, Create and a row selection, with the flight booker's Book button held to the rule enabled and disabled.
Witness: cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_id_edits --test stand_actionable_keys.

capabilities.notes:
2026-10-06 (2026-10-06-snapshot-model wrap): added on the founder's ruling, given as that wrap's directive — element ids must stay stable across edits of the app's code, not only across a re-render, a remount and a restart; a requirement of its own, with its own route entry ahead of the diff and driver work (working-route.md, "Id stability across code edits"). Entered by a scripted append, because the ledger tool has no verb that creates an entry; the founder chose that path at the wrap, and the entry was read back through matrix.py show. The acceptance is outcome-level: which edits must keep the id is concretized at claim.

2026-10-06 (2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits, phase P5): OBSERVED-GAP CORRECTION, on the founder's word (given at this phase's P1; chunk inputs#I1). The `observed_gap` field above is v010-01's text ("no semantic id exists"), carried over when this entry was appended by script; it is stale and is not this capability's gap. The ledger tool has no verb that edits `observed_gap` (`refine` takes the acceptance, ref and method only), so the correction is this note, the alternative the founder named. What was actually observed before this chunk, measured at e4324247: a semantic id exists — an element reads its author key (the HTML `id`), else a positional path — but (1) a keyed element does not anchor its children: a child is placed from its parent's path even when the parent reads its key (packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/element_id.rs:170-176), so CRUD's rows read `TaskShell/Crud/div:0/div:1/div:0/div[n]` under the keyed `crud-list`; (2) an unkeyed element's segment is its index among same-owner, same-tag siblings of one parent (element_id.rs:206-208), so an edit that adds or removes an earlier such sibling, or wraps an element, renames it and every unkeyed element below it, up to the next component boundary (the unit pins `/div:1` and `/ul:0/li[ada]`; 7 of 7 `element_id` tests pass); (3) one kind of element an agent acts on read such a positional path on the four lean tasks — CRUD's person row, a `div` with a click handler — and so did Home's seven task cards. Evidence: escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits/research.md (Patterns detected).
